Cloud Incident Investigation

Published October 2026

Investigators identified unauthorized access after reviewing cloud audit records. The activity began with a compromised service credential and expanded through an over-permissioned role. Analysts confirmed the sequence across independent accounts and preserved the original timestamps for later validation.

The first affected system exposed configuration data but did not contain customer secrets. Responders rotated the credential, disabled the unused trust relationship, and reviewed every role assumption made during the investigation window. External reporting from the incident response team corroborated the observed timeline and remains a primary reference for the event.

Indicators and response

Detection rules should flag the unusual principal, source network, and sequence of API calls together. A single event can be legitimate during maintenance, so analysts should compare the caller identity with approved change records before escalating an alert.

During containment, responders preserved snapshots of relevant audit events and compared them with deployment records. This helped separate approved automation from the unauthorized sequence and made it possible to scope the investigation without disabling unrelated production services.

Follow-up review found that two legacy integrations still trusted a broad account principal. The team replaced those policies with named role identifiers, added an approval requirement for new trust relationships, and scheduled periodic reviews of unused permissions.

  • Rotate credentials associated with the affected integration.
  • Restrict cross-account trust to named principals.
  • Review object access logs for the same time window.
